name: EDR Silencers / EDR Killer Tools
description: EDR killer tools — software designed to terminate, blind, or block telemetry from endpoint detection and response agents — have become a near-universal precursor step in ransomware intrusions. ESET's 2026 research catalogued nearly 90 distinct EDR killers in active use, including BYOVD (bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver) variants like EDRSandblast/EDRKillShifter and newer 'driverless' tools such as EDRSilencer and EDR-Freeze that abuse Windows Filtering Platform rules or process-freezing APIs instead of kernel drivers. EDRKillShifter, originally built by RansomHub, has since been adopted as shared affiliate tooling across Play, BianLian, Medusa, Qilin, DragonForce, BlackSuit, RansomHub, Crytox, Lynx, and INC ransomware operations. In April 2026, Cisco Talos detailed Qilin and Warlock affiliates using a customized EDRSandblast variant via a previously-unknown vulnerable driver (TPwSav.sys) capable of disabling 300+ EDR products in a four-stage infection chain immediately preceding encryptor deployment.

mitre_techniques.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
mitre_techniques.notes: EDR/AV agents are terminated, unloaded, or have their self-protection disabled prior to encryptor execution
Vulnerable signed drivers are loaded to gain kernel-level privileges needed to kill protected EDR processes
EDR killer payloads (e.g., EDRKillShifter loader) are packed/encrypted and decrypted only in memory at execution time

mitre_techniques.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
mitre_techniques.notes: Some EDR killers install a malicious or vulnerable driver as a kernel service to gain SYSTEM-level access
Often paired with EDR-killer deployment immediately before ransomware encryption and shadow copy deletion
PowerShell/batch scripts frequently used to drop and launch the EDR killer driver/loader pair

notable_examples: Cisco Talos (April 2026): Qilin and Warlock ransomware affiliates use a customized EDRSandblast variant exploiting the TPwSav.sys vulnerable driver to disable 300+ EDR products
ESET (March 2026): catalogued ~90 distinct EDR killer tools in the wild, noting reuse of drivers like BdApiUtil.sys and TfSysMon.sys across dead-av, TfSysMon-Killer, DLKiller, and Susanoo

EDRKillShifter, built originally for RansomHub, identified in August 2025 in simultaneous use by at least eight ransomware gangs: BlackSuit, RansomHub, Medusa, Qilin, DragonForce, Crytox, Lynx, and INC
Sophos 'Shared secret: EDR killer in the kill chain' report documenting cross-group sharing of a single EDR-killer binary among affiliate networks
Emergence of driverless EDR killers (EDRSilencer using WFP filters, EDR-Freeze suspending agent processes) reducing reliance on detectable vulnerable-driver loads
detection_opportunities: Alert on creation/loading of unsigned or known-vulnerable kernel drivers (check against the Microsoft/LOLDrivers vulnerable driver blocklist)
Monitor Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) for new filters that block EDR agent network communication (technique used by EDRSilencer)
Detect sudden EDR agent process termination, service stoppage, or loss of telemetry heartbeat across multiple endpoints in a short window
Enable and enforce tamper protection / self-defense features on all EDR agents, and alert on attempts to disable them
Hunt for process-suspend API calls (NtSuspendProcess) targeting EDR/AV processes, indicative of EDR-Freeze-style techniques
Treat any EDR outage or agent silence on a host as a high-priority incident — it frequently precedes ransomware encryption by minutes to hours
Apply Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist (HVCI/WDAC) to prevent loading of known BYOVD drivers used by EDR killers
